blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-migration-1 (rename_all camelCase silently renames the existing public JSON fields) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct OrderResponse {
    pub order_id: i64,
    pub customer_id: i64,
    pub total_cents: i64,
findings.recommendation: Remove `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` so `GET /orders/{id}` keeps emitting `order_id`, `customer_id` and `total_cents` (the new `currency` field is a single word and needs no rename). Today partners' integrations read `order_id`; after this change the JSON carries `orderId`, `customerId` and `totalCents`, so every partner reading the documented names gets a missing field on the first response after deploy. This is an unmarked breaking change: the release note only says "Added", and docs/api.md still lists the snake_case names and promises "a field is never renamed or removed without two releases of deprecation". If camelCase is really wanted, it needs a deprecation period (emit both names) and a **BREAKING** release note item.
findings.title: rename_all camelCase silently renames the existing public JSON fields

findings.evidence:
/// The currency of orders that do not name one (ISO 4217).
pub default_currency: String,
findings.recommendation: Give the field a default (`#[serde(default = "...")]` returning "EUR", the currency orders had before this change) so every deployed `config.toml` written for the previous version keeps loading. As written, `config::load` on an existing file with only `database_url` and `listen` fails with a missing-field error and the service does not start after the upgrade. Only config.example.toml was updated, and the release note does not tell operators to add the key. Add a test that loads the old two-key configuration.
findings.title: Existing config.toml files without default_currency no longer load
